newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain tries three for plotting to kill the king.
newsitem.headline: Spain tries three for plotting to kill the king.

text.p: Three suspected ETA Basque separatist guerrillas went on trial in Spain's high court on Wednesday accused of plotting to kill King Juan Carlos in 1995.

In dramatic testimony, two of the three -- Juan Jose Rego and Jorge Garcia -- related how they rented a flat on the island of Mallorca with a direct line of sight to the king's sailing yacht and how they had him in their rifle sights three times.
Garcia told the court he did not shoot the king because escape plans had not yet been finalised.

He and Rego described King Juan Carlos, Prince Felipe and Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar as "prime targets for ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom)", which has killed 800 people in a struggle for Basque region independence that began in 1968.
The third accused man, Rego's son Ignacio, said he knew nothing of the plot until he and Garcia were arrested in Palma de Mallorca in August, 1995, the state prosecutor told Spanish media.
Spaniards, who generally adore their king because of his down-to-earth style and his role in thwarting a 1981 coup attempt, were shocked to learn how close the guerrillas were to assassinating him.
The trial attracted a crowd of onlookers who heckled the accused and whistled as they left the court.
The three men are charged with plotting against the crown, belonging to an armed group, illegal possession of arms, storing explosives and falsification of official documents.
If convicted, they each face up to 39 years in prison.
According to the state prosecutor, Juan Jose Rego is a veteran member of ETA and has admitted to being the architect, on the orders of the rebel group's leadership, of the operation against the king.
The rebels usually target members of security forces, but they have also murdered politicians and government officials.
In May 1995, they came close to killing Aznar while he was still in opposition, setting off a powerful bomb that nearly destroyed his specially armoured car.

Rego told the court that he took part in the plot and he explained in detail how the attack was prepared, adding that he had unveiled the plans to the other two while they were travelling by rented boat to the island.
He said Garcia, whose task it was to shoot King Juan Carlos, had the king in his sights on three occasions, the last time on August 4 for 15 minutes.

Garcia testified that as a militant member of ETA, he had received orders to assassinate the king in Palma de Mallorca during the summer of 1995, accompanied by Juan Jose Rego and his son. He said ETA had supplied the rifle with a telescopic sight.
Garcia said Ignacio Rego was not guilty and had not taken part in the plot.
He said they had precise data about the movements of the royal family, who often spend their holidays at their summer palace on Mallorca, and their security services.
After the three accused men testified, they left the courtroom. Three port workers appeared next and said they had seen the accused in the area.
The arresting police officers also testified about the arms and explosives they had found in a search of the apartment.
The trial continues on Thursday.
